claim: A three-generation forward genetic screen in mice identified Megf8 as a novel modifier of BMP4 signaling in trigeminal ganglion (TG) neurons.
source: Using a three-generation forward genetic screen in mice we have identified Megf8 as a novel modifier of BMP4 signaling in trigeminal ganglion (TG) neurons.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a primary finding of the study.

claim: Loss of Megf8 disrupts axon guidance in the peripheral nervous system.
source: Loss of Megf8 disrupts axon guidance in the peripheral nervous system and leads to defects in development of the limb, heart, and left-right patterning, defects that resemble those observed in Bmp4 loss-of-function mice.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data showing TG axon defasciculation in Megf8 mutants.

claim: Loss of Megf8 leads to defects in development of the limb, heart, and left-right patterning.
source: Loss of Megf8 disrupts axon guidance in the peripheral nervous system and leads to defects in development of the limb, heart, and left-right patterning, defects that resemble those observed in Bmp4 loss-of-function mice.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental observations of polydactyly, heart defects, and reversed embryonic turning.

claim: Defects observed in Megf8 loss-of-function mice resemble those observed in Bmp4 loss-of-function mice.
source: Loss of Megf8 disrupts axon guidance in the peripheral nervous system and leads to defects in development of the limb, heart, and left-right patterning, defects that resemble those observed in Bmp4 loss-of-function mice.
evidence: This comparison is made explicitly in the abstract and supported by literature citations and experimental data.

claim: Bmp4 is expressed in a pattern that defines the permissive field for the peripheral projections of TG axons.
source: Bmp4 is expressed in a pattern that defines the permissive field for the peripheral projections of TG axons and mice lacking BMP signaling in sensory neurons exhibit TG axon defects that resemble those observed in Megf8−/− embryos.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by β-galactosidase staining showing Bmp4 expression patterns relative to TG axons.

claim: Mice lacking BMP signaling in sensory neurons exhibit TG axon defects that resemble those observed in Megf8−/− embryos.
source: Bmp4 is expressed in a pattern that defines the permissive field for the peripheral projections of TG axons and mice lacking BMP signaling in sensory neurons exhibit TG axon defects that resemble those observed in Megf8−/− embryos.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data from Wnt1-Cre;Bmpr2Flox/− mice showing ophthalmic nerve defasciculation.

claim: TG axon growth is robustly inhibited by BMP4.
source: Furthermore, TG axon growth is robustly inhibited by BMP4 and this inhibition is dependent on Megf8.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by in vitro TG explant assay data showing dose-dependent inhibition of axon outgrowth by BMP4.

claim: BMP4 inhibition of TG axon growth is dependent on Megf8.
source: Furthermore, TG axon growth is robustly inhibited by BMP4 and this inhibition is dependent on Megf8.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by explant assay data showing reduced BMP4 sensitivity in Megf8−/− TG explants.

claim: Megf8 is involved in mediating BMP4 signaling and guidance of developing TG axons.
source: Thus, our data suggest that Megf8 is involved in mediating BMP4 signaling and guidance of developing TG axons.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract, supported by multiple lines of experimental evidence.

claim: BMP signaling is an important regulator of sensory neuron development.
source: Bone morphogenetic protein (BMP) signaling has emerged as an important regulator of sensory neuron development.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: BMPs are members of the TGFβ superfamily of secreted growth factors.
source: BMPs are members of the TGFβ superfamily of secreted growth factors and are required for a wide range of developmental functions including gastrulation, mesoderm formation, neural patterning, left-right asymmetry, skeletal and limb development, kidney formation, and heart development (Zhao, 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: BMPs are required for gastrulation, mesoderm formation, neural patterning, left-right asymmetry, skeletal and limb development, kidney formation, and heart development.
source: BMPs are members of the TGFβ superfamily of secreted growth factors and are required for a wide range of developmental functions including gastrulation, mesoderm formation, neural patterning, left-right asymmetry, skeletal and limb development, kidney formation, and heart development (Zhao, 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: BMP7 in the spinal cord roof plate repels axons of developing commissural neurons.
source: BMP7 in the spinal cord roof plate repels axons of developing commissural neurons thus orienting their growth toward the floor plate (Augsburger et al., 1999; Butler and Dodd, 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: BMP4 is a target-derived cue that augments development of somatosensory neurons in the trigeminal ganglia (TG) and dorsal root ganglia (DRG).
source: Moreover, BMP4 is a target-derived cue that augments development of somatosensory neurons in the trigeminal ganglia (TG) and dorsal root ganglia (DRG).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by subsequent citations.

claim: BMP4 is expressed in the developing craniofacial region and signals retrogradely to coordinate differential gene expression and patterning along the dorsoventral axis of the trigeminal ganglion.
source: BMP4 is expressed in the developing craniofacial region and signals retrogradely to coordinate differential gene expression and patterning along the dorsoventral axis of the trigeminal ganglion (Hodge et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: BMP4 appears to have a trophic effect on TG and DRG neurons.
source: Furthermore, BMP4 appears to have a trophic effect on TG and DRG neurons as altering the level of BMP4 expression in the skin leads to changes in the peripheral innervation and number of sensory neurons found in both the TG and DRG (Guha et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Altering the level of BMP4 expression in the skin leads to changes in the peripheral innervation and number of sensory neurons found in both the TG and DRG.
source: Furthermore, BMP4 appears to have a trophic effect on TG and DRG neurons as altering the level of BMP4 expression in the skin leads to changes in the peripheral innervation and number of sensory neurons found in both the TG and DRG (Guha et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Line 687 exhibits severe defasciculation of the ophthalmic branch of the trigeminal nerve.
source: One of the mutant mouse lines, Line 687, exhibits severe defasciculation of the ophthalmic branch of the trigeminal nerve.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by neurofilament staining images.

claim: In Line 687 mutants, the two major branches of the ophthalmic nerve initially form properly as tightly bound fascicles; however, as the axons extend into the target field, they prematurely defasciculate within the face.
source: In Line 687 mutants, the two major branches of the ophthalmic nerve initially form properly as tightly bound fascicles; however, as the axons extend into the target field, they prematurely defasciculate within the face (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1A showing neurofilament staining.

claim: The genetic lesion responsible for the phenotype in Line 687 was mapped to a 2.6 Mb region of Chromosome 7 between rs3715453 and D7JHMI24 that contains 76 open reading frames.
source: We mapped the genetic lesion responsible for the phenotype in Line 687 to a 2.6 Mb region of Chromosome 7 between rs3715453 and D7JHMI24 that contains 76 open reading frames (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1B showing the mapping data.

claim: A single base pair substitution, 5324T>C, was identified in the gene Megf8 in Line 687.
source: This analysis revealed a single base pair substitution, 5324T>C, in the gene multiple EGF-like-domains 8 (Megf8) (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1C showing sequence data.

claim: Megf8 is a very large putative transmembrane protein with a signal peptide, a CUB domain, plexin-semaphorin-integrin (PSI) domains, Kelch domains, EGF/EGF-like domains, and a C-terminal transmembrane domain.
source: Megf8 is a very large putative transmembrane protein, and it is predicted to have a signal peptide, a CUB domain, plexin-semaphorin-integrin (PSI) domains, Kelch domains, EGF/EGF-like domains, and a C-terminal transmembrane domain.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on bioinformatic analysis.

claim: The mutation in Line 687 (Megf8L1775P) encodes a single L>P amino acid substitution (L1775P) in the fourth Kelch domain of Megf8.
source: The mutation in Line 687 (Megf8L1775P) is predicted to encode a single L>P amino acid substitution (L1775P) in the fourth Kelch domain of Megf8 (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1D showing the protein structure.

claim: Megf8L1775P/Trap embryos phenocopy the Megf8L1775P/L1775P mutants and show defasciculation of the TG ophthalmic nerve.
source: Megf8L1775P/Trap embryos phenocopy the Megf8L1775P/L1775P mutants and show defasciculation of the TG ophthalmic nerve (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The Line 687 TG phenotype results from the Megf8L1775P mutation.
source: These results confirm that the Line 687 TG phenotype results from the Megf8L1775P mutation and demonstrate that Megf8 is required for proper growth and guidance of the TG ophthalmic nerve.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on complementation analysis.

claim: Megf8 is required for proper growth and guidance of the TG ophthalmic nerve.
source: These results confirm that the Line 687 TG phenotype results from the Megf8L1775P mutation and demonstrate that Megf8 is required for proper growth and guidance of the TG ophthalmic nerve.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on complementation analysis and phenotypic observations.

claim: Megf8 is widely expressed during early embryonic development.
source: Whole-mount ISH of E8.5–E10.5 embryos showed that Megf8 is widely expressed, with strong expression in the somites, limb buds, primordial gut, developing eye, and in the pharyngeal arches (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2A-C showing in situ hybridization.

claim: Megf8 is strongly expressed in the somites, limb buds, primordial gut, developing eye, and pharyngeal arches.
source: Whole-mount ISH of E8.5–E10.5 embryos showed that Megf8 is widely expressed, with strong expression in the somites, limb buds, primordial gut, developing eye, and in the pharyngeal arches (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2A-C.

claim: Megf8 is highly expressed in the developing nervous system.
source: Megf8 is also highly expressed in the developing nervous system.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by in situ hybridization data.

claim: Sensory neurons of the DRG and TG show strong expression of Megf8 throughout embryogenesis and into the postnatal period.
source: Sensory neurons of the DRG and TG show strong expression of Megf8 throughout embryogenesis and into the postnatal period (Figure 2D,E, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figures 2D, 2E, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Megf8 is expressed in the CNS including the developing neuroepithelium, postnatal hippocampus, layer 4/5 of the cortex, and the olfactory bulb.
source: Megf8 is also expressed in the CNS including the developing neuroepithelium (Figure 2F), postnatal hippocampus, layer 4/5 of the cortex, and the olfactory bulb (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2F and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Megf8−/− embryos phenocopy Megf8L1775P/L1775P embryos and exhibit dramatic defasciculation and undergrowth of the ophthalmic branch of the trigeminal nerve.
source: Megf8−/− embryos phenocopy Megf8L1775P/L1775P embryos and exhibit dramatic defasciculation and undergrowth of the ophthalmic branch of the trigeminal nerve (Figures 3A and 4H).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figures 3A and 4H.

claim: In both the Megf8 null and Megf8L1775P/L1775P lines the maxillary and mandibular branches of the TG are largely unaffected.
source: In both the Megf8 null and Megf8L1775P/L1775P lines the maxillary and mandibular branches of the TG are largely unaffected.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by quantification data in Figure 4H legend.

claim: Both Megf8−/− and Megf8L1775P/L1775P embryos display polydactyly in both the forelimbs and hindlimbs.
source: Both Megf8−/− and Megf8L1775P/L1775P embryos display polydactyly in both the forelimbs and hindlimbs; this pre-axial polydactyly is completely penetrant, and embryos show six to seven digits per limb as well as duplication of bones in the hand (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Pre-axial polydactyly in Megf8 mutants is completely penetrant, and embryos show six to seven digits per limb as well as duplication of bones in the hand.
source: Both Megf8−/− and Megf8L1775P/L1775P embryos display polydactyly in both the forelimbs and hindlimbs; this pre-axial polydactyly is completely penetrant, and embryos show six to seven digits per limb as well as duplication of bones in the hand (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Megf8 mutants exhibit skeletal abnormalities including delayed ossification of the rib cage, a wider and shorter rib cage, and a split sternum.
source: They also exhibit skeletal abnormalities including delayed ossification of the rib cage, a wider and shorter rib cage, and a split sternum (Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Loss of Megf8 leads to a disruption of left-right patterning.
source: Furthermore, loss of Megf8 leads to a disruption of left-right patterning.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by observations of reversed heart looping and embryonic turning.

claim: Approximately one third of Megf8−/− embryos demonstrate a complete left-right inversion of heart looping or embryonic turning.
source: Approximately one third of Megf8−/− embryos demonstrate a complete left-right inversion of heart looping (Figure 3D) or embryonic turning (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figures 3D and 3E, as well as Table 1 showing penetrance data.

claim: Megf8 is required for development of left-right asymmetry.
source: Taken together with prior results, these findings indicate that Megf8 is required for development of left-right asymmetry.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on observed phenotypes and comparison with prior results.

claim: Megf8 is required for normal heart development.
source: In addition to its role in development of the limb, skeleton, and left-right asymmetry, Megf8 is also required for normal heart development.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by detailed descriptions of heart defects.

claim: Loss of Megf8 function leads to a complete, or nearly complete, absence of the mitral and tricuspid valves, swollen atria, transposition of the outflow tract, pulmonary stenosis, and atrial and ventricular septal defects.
source: In addition to the inversion of heart looping observed in some Megf8−/− and Megf8L1775P/L1775P embryos, loss of Megf8 function leads to a complete, or nearly complete, absence of the mitral and tricuspid valves, swollen atria, transposition of the outflow tract, pulmonary stenosis, and atrial and ventricular septal defects (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: Heart phenotypes in Megf8 mutants were seen in all embryos at E14.5 or later, and they lead to severe peripheral edema and embryonic lethality by age E16.5.
source: These phenotypes were seen in all embryos at E14.5 or later, and they lead to severe peripheral edema (Figure 3F) and embryonic lethality by age E16.5.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3F.

claim: Analysis at earlier stages revealed apparently normal endocardial cushion mesenchymal cells in Megf8 mutants.
source: Analysis at earlier stages revealed apparently normal endocardial cushion mesenchymal cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 3), which implies that the terminal pathologies result from improper remodeling events after E12.5.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: The terminal heart pathologies in Megf8 mutants result from improper remodeling events after E12.5.
source: Analysis at earlier stages revealed apparently normal endocardial cushion mesenchymal cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 3), which implies that the terminal pathologies result from improper remodeling events after E12.5.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of normal early structures but abnormal later structures.

claim: Conditional mutation of the Megf8Flox allele using the Mesp1-Cre line did not cause any heart phenotypes.
source: Conditional mutation of the Megf8Flox allele using the Mesp1-Cre line (Saga et al., 1999), which is active in all mesoderm of the heart, did not cause any heart phenotypes (data not shown), implying that early heart and embryo laterality defects might be responsible for the constellation of later heart defects.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: Early heart and embryo laterality defects might be responsible for the constellation of later heart defects in Megf8 mutants.
source: Conditional mutation of the Megf8Flox allele using the Mesp1-Cre line (Saga et al., 1999), which is active in all mesoderm of the heart, did not cause any heart phenotypes (data not shown), implying that early heart and embryo laterality defects might be responsible for the constellation of later heart defects.
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of heart phenotypes when Megf8 is deleted specifically in heart mesoderm.

claim: A second mouse line harboring a Megf8 point mutation (Megf8C193R) was identified in an independent forward genetic screen and has polydactyly and defects in left-right patterning and heart development.
source: These findings are consistent with a second mouse line harboring a Megf8 point mutation (Megf8C193R) that was identified in an independent forward genetic screen and which was shown to have polydactyly and defects in left-right patterning and heart development (Zhang et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by a citation.

claim: In Megf8−/− embryos, spinal nerves are shorter at E11.5 than in wild type.
source: In Megf8−/− embryos, spinal nerves are shorter at E11.5 than in wild type (Figure 4A,D), and by E13.5 the radial and ulnar nerves have not fully extended into the limbs, appearing shorter and less branched (Figure 4B,E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figures 4A and 4D.

claim: By E13.5 the radial and ulnar nerves in Megf8−/− embryos have not fully extended into the limbs, appearing shorter and less branched.
source: In Megf8−/− embryos, spinal nerves are shorter at E11.5 than in wild type (Figure 4A,D), and by E13.5 the radial and ulnar nerves have not fully extended into the limbs, appearing shorter and less branched (Figure 4B,E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figures 4B and 4E.

claim: At E13.5 the limbs appear immature in Megf8−/− embryos relative to wild type littermates.
source: At E13.5 the limbs appear immature in Megf8−/− embryos relative to wild type littermates, which may contribute to the radial and ulnar nerve phenotypes.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on morphological observations.

claim: Megf8−/− embryos display defects in the developing vagus and glossopharyngeal nerves.
source: Megf8−/− embryos also display defects in the developing vagus and glossopharyngeal nerves.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by neurofilament staining data.

claim: At E11.5 the vagus and glossopharyngeal nerves in Megf8−/− embryos are slightly defasciculated and several wayward axons branch away from the main fiber bundle.
source: At E11.5 these nerves are slightly defasciculated and several wayward axons branch away from the main fiber bundle (Figure 4C,F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figures 4C and 4F.

claim: Megf8 is required for proper axonal extension in several areas of the PNS, including the TG, DRG, and vagus/glossopharyngeal nerves.
source: Overall, these findings demonstrate that Megf8 is required for proper axonal extension in several areas of the PNS, including the TG, DRG, and vagus/glossopharyngeal nerves (Table 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Table 1 summarizing phenotypes.

claim: Wnt1-Cre-mediated conditional deletion of Megf8 leads to defasciculation of the ophthalmic branch of the trigeminal nerve, phenocopying Megf8−/− and Megf8L1775P/L1775P mutant embryos.
source: Wnt1-Cre-mediated conditional deletion of Megf8 leads to defasciculation of the ophthalmic branch of the trigeminal nerve, phenocopying Megf8−/− and Megf8L1775P/L1775P mutant embryos (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 4G.

claim: Megf8 mediates guidance of developing TG axons in a cell autonomous manner.
source: These findings suggest that Megf8 mediates guidance of developing TG axons in a cell autonomous manner.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on Wnt1-Cre conditional deletion experiments.

claim: Wnt1-Cre;Megf8Flox/Flox embryos do not exhibit a defect in radial/ulnar nerve development.
source: Wnt1-Cre;Megf8Flox/Flox embryos do not exhibit a defect in radial/ulnar nerve development, however, suggesting that Megf8's role in spinal nerve axon guidance is non-cell autonomous (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Megf8's role in spinal nerve axon guidance is non-cell autonomous.
source: Wnt1-Cre;Megf8Flox/Flox embryos do not exhibit a defect in radial/ulnar nerve development, however, suggesting that Megf8's role in spinal nerve axon guidance is non-cell autonomous (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on the lack of radial/ulnar nerve phenotype in Wnt1-Cre conditional mutants.

claim: The spectrum of phenotypes seen in Megf8−/− embryos is strikingly similar to that observed when BMP signaling is disrupted.
source: The spectrum of phenotypes seen in Megf8−/− embryos is strikingly similar to that observed when BMP signaling is disrupted (Table 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Table 1 comparing phenotypes.

claim: Loss of BMP4, and to a lesser extent BMP2 and BMP7, results in similar defects as those observed in the Megf8 mutants.
source: We noted that loss of BMP4, and to a lesser extent BMP2 and BMP7, results in similar defects as those observed in the Megf8 mutants.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by citations to BMP loss-of-function studies.

claim: Bmp4 and Bmp7 loss-of-function mouse lines exhibit pre-axial polydactyly.
source: Bmp4 and Bmp7 loss-of-function mouse lines exhibit pre-axial polydactyly (Dudley et al., 1995; Luo et al., 1995; Dunn et al., 1997; Selever et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by citations.

claim: Bmp4 null embryos display disrupted left-right patterning and loss of normal rightward heart looping.
source: Bmp4 null embryos also display disrupted left-right patterning and loss of normal rightward heart looping (Fujiwara et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by a citation.

claim: Loss of BMP4, or its receptor BMPR2, results in a wide range of heart defects, including atrial septal defects, ventricular septal defects, atrioventricular septal defects, and abnormal positioning or septation of the outflow tract.
source: Loss of BMP4, or its receptor BMPR2, results in a wide range of heart defects, including atrial septal defects, ventricular septal defects, atrioventricular septal defects, and abnormal positioning or septation of the outflow tract (Jiao et al., 2003; Liu et al., 2004; Beppu et al., 2009); several of these cardiac phenotypes are exacerbated by a concomitant loss of BMP2 or BMP7 (Rivera-Feliciano and Tabin, 2006; Goldman et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by citations.

claim: BMP4 signaling is required for dorsoventral patterning of the TG.
source: Furthermore, BMP4 signaling is required for dorsoventral patterning of the TG (Hodge et al., 2007), and modifying BMP4 expression in the skin leads to changes in the peripheral innervation and survival of sensory neurons (Guha et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by a citation.

claim: Modifying BMP4 expression in the skin leads to changes in the peripheral innervation and survival of sensory neurons.
source: Furthermore, BMP4 signaling is required for dorsoventral patterning of the TG (Hodge et al., 2007), and modifying BMP4 expression in the skin leads to changes in the peripheral innervation and survival of sensory neurons (Guha et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by a citation.

claim: At E10.5, Bmp4 is expressed strongly in the eye and also in the dorsal portion of the face above the eye.
source: At E10.5, Bmp4 is expressed strongly in the eye and also in the dorsal portion of the face above the eye (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5A showing β-galactosidase staining.

claim: The two areas of BMP4 expression at E10.5 flank a narrow corridor through which the developing ophthalmic nerve projects.
source: These two areas of BMP4 expression flank a narrow corridor through which the developing ophthalmic nerve projects; this expression pattern suggests that BMP4 may act as a repulsive guidance cue for developing TG axons.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on the spatial relationship between Bmp4 expression and TG axons.

claim: The expression pattern of Bmp4 suggests that BMP4 may act as a repulsive guidance cue for developing TG axons.
source: These two areas of BMP4 expression flank a narrow corridor through which the developing ophthalmic nerve projects; this expression pattern suggests that BMP4 may act as a repulsive guidance cue for developing TG axons.
evidence: This is inferred from the spatial relationship between Bmp4 expression and TG axon trajectories.

claim: At E11.5, as the ophthalmic branch extends beyond the eye, the nasociliary nerve branches in a region devoid of Bmp4 expression and then immediately projects nasally as a tightly bundled fascicle through an area of strong Bmp4 expression.
source: One day later, at E11.5, the TG axons have extended into their peripheral targets and have bifurcated into frontal and nasociliary nerves. At this stage, Bmp4 expression is striking; as the ophthalmic branch extends beyond the eye, the nasociliary nerve branches in a region devoid of Bmp4 expression and then immediately projects nasally as a tightly bundled fascicle through an area of strong Bmp4 expression while the axons of the frontal branch extend rostrally.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on β-galactosidase and neurofilament co-staining.

claim: The pattern of Bmp4 expression is disrupted in Megf8−/− embryos.
source: Remarkably, the pattern of Bmp4 expression is disrupted in Megf8−/− embryos.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by β-galactosidase staining data.

claim: In the absence of Megf8, Bmp4 expression is lost at the point of defasciculation of the ophthalmic branch into the frontal and nasociliary branches.
source: In the absence of Megf8, Bmp4 expression is lost at the point of defasciculation of the ophthalmic branch into the frontal and nasociliary branches (Figure 5B; Table 1) suggesting that axonal innervation of the target region is necessary for proper expression of Bmp4 and that the absence of this BMP signaling leads to defasciculation of the nasociliary branch of the ophthalmic nerve.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5B and Table 1.

claim: Axonal innervation of the target region is necessary for proper expression of Bmp4.
source: In the absence of Megf8, Bmp4 expression is lost at the point of defasciculation of the ophthalmic branch into the frontal and nasociliary branches (Figure 5B; Table 1) suggesting that axonal innervation of the target region is necessary for proper expression of Bmp4 and that the absence of this BMP signaling leads to defasciculation of the nasociliary branch of the ophthalmic nerve.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Bmp4 expression is lost where axons defasciculate in Megf8 mutants.

claim: The absence of BMP signaling leads to defasciculation of the nasociliary branch of the ophthalmic nerve.
source: In the absence of Megf8, Bmp4 expression is lost at the point of defasciculation of the ophthalmic branch into the frontal and nasociliary branches (Figure 5B; Table 1) suggesting that axonal innervation of the target region is necessary for proper expression of Bmp4 and that the absence of this BMP signaling leads to defasciculation of the nasociliary branch of the ophthalmic nerve.
evidence: This is inferred from the correlation between loss of Bmp4 expression and axon defasciculation.

claim: In Megf8−/− embryos Bmp4 expression is disrupted exclusively in the area around the ophthalmic branch but is intact throughout the rest of the embryo.
source: Interestingly, in Megf8−/− embryos Bmp4 expression is disrupted exclusively in the area around the ophthalmic branch but is intact throughout the rest of the embryo (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Bmpr2 is robustly expressed in all three lobes of the developing TG.
source: Bmpr2 is robustly expressed in all three lobes of the developing TG, as is Megf8 (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 2 showing in situ hybridization.

claim: The ophthalmic branch of the trigeminal nerve in E11.5 Wnt1-Cre;Bmpr2Flox/− embryos is stunted and branches prematurely in a manner reminiscent of the phenotype seen in Megf8 loss-of-function lines.
source: Interestingly, the ophthalmic branch of the trigeminal nerve in E11.5 Wnt1-Cre;Bmpr2Flox/− embryos is stunted and branches prematurely in a manner reminiscent of the phenotype seen in Megf8 loss-of-function lines (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5C.

claim: The maxillary and mandibular branches of the trigeminal nerve are unaffected in the Wnt1-Cre;Bmpr2Flox/− embryos.
source: Furthermore, the maxillary and mandibular branches of the trigeminal nerve are unaffected in the Wnt1-Cre;Bmpr2Flox/− embryos, as in Megf8 null lines.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: BMP signaling is required specifically for development of the ophthalmic branch of the trigeminal nerve.
source: These results demonstrate that BMP signaling is required specifically for development of the ophthalmic branch of the trigeminal nerve, and they suggest that both Megf8 and BMPR2 are necessary to mediate this signaling.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on the Wnt1-Cre;Bmpr2Flox/− phenotype.

claim: Both Megf8 and BMPR2 are necessary to mediate BMP signaling in the ophthalmic branch of the trigeminal nerve.
source: These results demonstrate that BMP signaling is required specifically for development of the ophthalmic branch of the trigeminal nerve, and they suggest that both Megf8 and BMPR2 are necessary to mediate this signaling.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on the similar phenotypes of Megf8 and Bmpr2 mutants.

claim: BMP4 robustly inhibits the outgrowth of wild-type TG axons.
source: Remarkably, BMP4 robustly inhibits the outgrowth of wild-type TG axons, and maximal doses inhibit axon outgrowth by more than 50% (Figure 6A,C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figures 6A and 6C showing explant assay data.

claim: Maximal doses of BMP4 inhibit TG axon outgrowth by more than 50%.
source: Remarkably, BMP4 robustly inhibits the outgrowth of wild-type TG axons, and maximal doses inhibit axon outgrowth by more than 50% (Figure 6A,C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figures 6A and 6C.

claim: Megf8−/− explants exhibit significantly greater axon outgrowth in the presence of BMP4, but not under control culture conditions.
source: Megf8−/− explants exhibit significantly greater axon outgrowth in the presence of BMP4, but not under control culture conditions (Figure 6B,D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figures 6B and 6D.

claim: Megf8−/− axons are less sensitive to the inhibitory effects of BMP4.
source: These results demonstrate that Megf8−/− axons are less sensitive to the inhibitory effects of BMP4 and that the response of TG neurons to BMP4 is partially dependent on Megf8 expression.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on explant assay data.

claim: The response of TG neurons to BMP4 is partially dependent on Megf8 expression.
source: These results demonstrate that Megf8−/− axons are less sensitive to the inhibitory effects of BMP4 and that the response of TG neurons to BMP4 is partially dependent on Megf8 expression.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on explant assay data.

claim: Megf8 functions within TG sensory axons, allowing them to respond to intermediate target-derived BMP4 and thus guide these axons to their appropriate peripheral target regions in the face.
source: Together with our in vivo findings, these results support a model in which Megf8 functions within TG sensory axons, allowing them to respond to intermediate target-derived BMP4 and thus guide these axons to their appropriate peripheral target regions in the face.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the combined in vivo and in vitro data.

claim: Megf8 regulates development of the limb, skeleton, heart, left-right asymmetry, and PNS.
source: Analysis of Megf8L1775P/L1775P and Megf8−/− embryos demonstrates that Megf8 functions broadly during embryogenesis and is required for the development of several organ systems.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section summarizing the findings.

claim: Loss of Megf8 function leads to pre-axial polydactyly, skeletal defects, disruption of left-right patterning, and severe heart defects, all of which together result in embryonic lethality.
source: Loss of Megf8 function leads to pre-axial polydactyly, skeletal defects, disruption of left-right patterning, and severe heart defects, all of which together result in embryonic lethality (present study, and Zhang et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by data from the present study and a citation.

claim: Mutations in Megf8 were recently identified in a small subset of children with Carpenter syndrome.
source: Interestingly, mutations in Megf8 were recently identified in a small subset of children with Carpenter syndrome, which is an autosomal-recessive multiple-congenital-malformation disorder.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by a citation.

claim: Carpenter syndrome is an autosomal-recessive multiple-congenital-malformation disorder.
source: Interestingly, mutations in Megf8 were recently identified in a small subset of children with Carpenter syndrome, which is an autosomal-recessive multiple-congenital-malformation disorder.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section.

claim: Mutations in Megf8 in Carpenter syndrome patients resulted in thoracic skeletal defects, limb defects such as pre-axial polydactyly, congenital heart defects, and profound lateralization defects including transposition of the great arteries, dextrocardia, and complete situs inversus.
source: Mutations were identified in several domains of Megf8, including the Kelch domain adjacent to the Kelch domain harboring the L1775P point mutation, and resulted in thoracic skeletal defects, limb defects such as pre-axial polydactyly, congenital heart defects, and profound lateralization defects including transposition of the great arteries, dextrocardia, and complete situs inversus (Twigg et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by a citation.

claim: Phenotypes in Carpenter syndrome patients with Megf8 mutations mirror those seen in Megf8 loss-of-function mouse lines.
source: These phenotypes mirror those seen in our Megf8 loss-of-function lines and reinforce the vital role for Megf8 throughout embryogenesis.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section comparing human and mouse phenotypes.

claim: Megf8 is required for development of the peripheral nervous system, including the growth and guidance of the TG, spinal, and vagus/glossopharyngeal nerves.
source: Megf8 is also required for development of the peripheral nervous system, including the growth and guidance of the TG, spinal, and vagus/glossopharyngeal nerves.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section summarizing the findings.

claim: Megf8−/− embryos exhibit profound defasciculation of the ophthalmic branch of the TG, undergrown and underbranched spinal nerves, and defasciculation of the vagus/glossopharyngeal nerves.
source: Megf8−/− embryos exhibit profound defasciculation of the ophthalmic branch of the TG, undergrown and underbranched spinal nerves, and defasciculation of the vagus/glossopharyngeal nerves.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section summarizing the findings.

claim: Megf8 is strongly expressed in sensory neurons throughout embryogenesis.
source: Megf8 is strongly expressed in sensory neurons throughout embryogenesis, and conditional deletion of Megf8 in neural crest-derived cells, including sensory neurons (Wnt1-Cre;Megf8Flox/Flox), leads to a defect in the TG ophthalmic nerve that phenocopies the Megf8 null and Megf8L1775P/L1775P lines.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section summarizing the findings.

claim: Conditional deletion of Megf8 in neural crest-derived cells leads to a defect in the TG ophthalmic nerve that phenocopies the Megf8 null and Megf8L1775P/L1775P lines.
source: Megf8 is strongly expressed in sensory neurons throughout embryogenesis, and conditional deletion of Megf8 in neural crest-derived cells, including sensory neurons (Wnt1-Cre;Megf8Flox/Flox), leads to a defect in the TG ophthalmic nerve that phenocopies the Megf8 null and Megf8L1775P/L1775P lines.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section summarizing the findings.

claim: Megf8 functions cell autonomously in TG neurons to regulate axon guidance and innervation of peripheral targets.
source: These results strongly suggest that Megf8 functions cell autonomously in TG neurons to regulate axon guidance and innervation of peripheral targets.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on conditional deletion experiments.

claim: Megf8 is a component of the BMP4 signaling pathway.
source: Given these phenotypic similarities, we hypothesized that Megf8 is a component of the BMP4 signaling pathway and specifically regulates the response of TG neurons to target-derived BMP4.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a hypothesis based on phenotypic similarities.

claim: Megf8 specifically regulates the response of TG neurons to target-derived BMP4.
source: Given these phenotypic similarities, we hypothesized that Megf8 is a component of the BMP4 signaling pathway and specifically regulates the response of TG neurons to target-derived BMP4.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a hypothesis.

claim: Bmp4 expression appears to define the permissible field for ophthalmic nerve target innervation.
source: We assessed Bmp4 expression during E10.5–E11.5, which is the period when TG axons extend into their peripheral target fields and found that Bmp4 expression appears to define the permissible field for ophthalmic nerve target innervation suggesting that BMP4 may function as a repulsive guidance cue.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on Bmp4 expression analysis.

claim: BMP4 may function as a repulsive guidance cue for TG axons.
source: We assessed Bmp4 expression during E10.5–E11.5, which is the period when TG axons extend into their peripheral target fields and found that Bmp4 expression appears to define the permissible field for ophthalmic nerve target innervation suggesting that BMP4 may function as a repulsive guidance cue.
evidence: This is inferred from the spatial relationship between Bmp4 expression and TG axon trajectories.

claim: Axons of TG ophthalmic sensory neurons require both Megf8 and BMP signaling to correctly navigate towards their target field.
source: Thus, axons of TG ophthalmic sensory neurons require both Megf8 and BMP signaling to correctly navigate towards their target field.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on the phenotypes of Megf8 and Bmpr2 mutants.

claim: Megf8 and BMPR2 function selectively in neurons of the TG ophthalmic branch to mediate axon guidance.
source: Remarkably, in each of the Megf8 and Bmpr2 loss-of-function lines, the TG maxillary and mandibular branches are largely unaffected despite widespread expression of Megf8 and BMPR2 within the TG ganglion, which demonstrates that Megf8 and BMPR2 function selectively in neurons of the TG ophthalmic branch to mediate axon guidance.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on the selective phenotype in the ophthalmic branch.

claim: Megf8 is a mediator or a key component of the BMPR2 signaling pathways that control growth and guidance of ophthalmic nerve axons.
source: We suggest that Megf8 is a mediator or a key component of the BMPR2 signaling pathways that control growth and guidance of ophthalmic nerve axons.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a conclusion from the data.

claim: BMP4 acts as an inhibitory cue to prevent developing TG axons from innervating inappropriate targets.
source: The expression pattern of Bmp4 relative to the developing ophthalmic nerve suggests that BMP4 acts as an inhibitory cue to prevent developing TG axons from innervating inappropriate targets.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on Bmp4 expression patterns and in vitro data.

claim: This hypothesized role for BMP4 as an inhibitory cue is supported by in vitro findings showing BMP4 treatment of TG explant cultures resulted in robust inhibition of axon outgrowth.
source: This hypothesized role for BMP4 is supported by our in vitro findings, in which BMP4 treatment of TG explant cultures resulted in robust inhibition of axon outgrowth.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section connecting the hypothesis to experimental data.

claim: Inhibition of TG axon outgrowth by BMP4 was partially lost in Megf8−/− explants, indicating that TG neurons require Megf8 expression to mediate their maximal response to the inhibitory effects of BMP4.
source: This inhibition was partially lost in Megf8−/− explants, indicating that TG neurons require Megf8 expression to mediate their maximal response to the inhibitory effects of BMP4.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on explant assay data.

claim: TG neurons require Megf8 expression to mediate their maximal response to the inhibitory effects of BMP4.
source: This inhibition was partially lost in Megf8−/− explants, indicating that TG neurons require Megf8 expression to mediate their maximal response to the inhibitory effects of BMP4.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on explant assay data.

claim: Megf8 is necessary for BMP4 signaling in sensory neurons.
source: These findings suggest that Megf8 is necessary for BMP4 signaling in sensory neurons and that this signaling provides an important inhibitory cue to guide developing TG axons.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a conclusion from the data.

claim: BMP4 signaling provides an important inhibitory cue to guide developing TG axons.
source: These findings suggest that Megf8 is necessary for BMP4 signaling in sensory neurons and that this signaling provides an important inhibitory cue to guide developing TG axons.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a conclusion from the data.

claim: Bmp4 expression is dependent on signaling from incoming TG axons.
source: In addition, our finding that Bmp4 expression is disrupted in Megf8−/− embryos at the site of defasciculation of the TG ophthalmic branch suggests a possible non-cell autonomous role for Megf8 in regulating Bmp4 expression, wherein BMP4 expression is dependent on signaling from incoming TG axons, which is disrupted by defasciculation in the Megf8−/− embryo.
evidence: This is suggested as a possible explanation for the disrupted Bmp4 expression in Megf8 mutants.

claim: Megf8 is a mediator of BMP4 signaling in TG axons.
source: Taken together, our findings support a model in which Megf8 is a mediator of BMP4 signaling in TG axons.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as the main conclusion.

claim: Megf8 is expressed in TG sensory neurons where it acts cell autonomously to promote signaling in response to target-derived BMP4.
source: Megf8 is expressed in TG sensory neurons where it acts cell autonomously to promote signaling in response to target-derived BMP4.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as part of the proposed model.

claim: Megf8-mediated BMP4 signaling, which is inhibitory for TG axons, likely enables these axons to remain fasciculated en route to their appropriate targets in the face.
source: Megf8-mediated BMP4 signaling, which is inhibitory for TG axons, likely enables these axons to remain fasciculated en route to their appropriate targets in the face.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as part of the proposed model.

claim: Disruption of Megf8-mediated BMP4 signaling leads to a corresponding loss of inhibition and premature defasciculation of the nerve.
source: Disruption of this signaling, either through loss of Megf8 or other components of the BMP4 pathway, leads to a corresponding loss of inhibition and premature defasciculation of the nerve.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as part of the proposed model.

claim: BMP4 signaling is required for TG axon guidance.
source: Thus, BMP4 signaling is required for TG axon guidance and Megf8 is a novel component of BMP4 signaling in TG sensory neurons.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a conclusion.

claim: Megf8 is a novel component of BMP4 signaling in TG sensory neurons.
source: Thus, BMP4 signaling is required for TG axon guidance and Megf8 is a novel component of BMP4 signaling in TG sensory neurons.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a conclusion.

claim: Megf8 mediates signaling by BMP4 and, perhaps, other TGFβ family members throughout the embryo during development.
source: Given the numerous phenotypic similarities between Megf8 and Bmp loss-of-function mouse lines, including defects in the limb, heart, and left-right patterning, we propose that Megf8 mediates signaling by BMP4 and, perhaps, other TGFβ family members throughout the embryo during development.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a broader proposal based on the phenotypic similarities.

claim: BMPR2 is one of several BMP receptors and is preferentially activated by BMP ligands and not by other TGF-β superfamily members.
source: BMPR2, one of several BMP receptors, is preferentially activated by BMP ligands and not by other TGF-β superfamily members (Miyazono et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by a citation.
